label: Photoresist grating coupler (period about 0.665 um) on an rf-sputtered dense flint glass film waveguide, He-Ne 6328 Angstrom
core_material: rf-sputtered Corning 8390 dense flint glass film (n about 1.73) on a Corning 8370 glass substrate (n 1.515); grating of Shipley AZ-1350 photoresist formed directly on the film
notes: Grating formed by exposing the photoresist to a 4880 Angstrom laser interferometer fringe pattern and developing it (p.3); passive wording, no org named: fab empty (D80b). Input is a free-space laser beam (about 2 mm diameter) aimed at the grating near its edge, not a fiber: class fiber_chip_coupler.grating follows the D971 ruling for the tien1969 prism coupler (coupler into an on-chip thin-film guide) and the papers.csv class hint. Film index 1.72 +/- 0.03 from in-situ microprobe analysis (p.4) and the fitted index 1.73 (p.3) not entered (no film-index parameter). Coupling angles printed in Fig. 2 (TE 48.4 and 41.4 deg, TM 48.0 and 40.3 deg) kept in conditions; the TE0 / TE1 assignment of the two TE angles follows the dip positions in Fig. 3 (TE1 near 41.5 deg, TE0 near 48.5 deg). Not entered (no registry parameter): angular widths of the coupling dips labelled in Fig. 3 (0.25 deg TE1, 0.08 deg TE0). TM coupling observed (p.3) but no efficiency stated for it.

label: Uncoated Fabry-Perot GaAs-AlxGa1-xAs double-heterostructure junction laser, 370 um x about 80 um, diamond heat sink, CW at room temperature
core_material: four-layer LPE structure on (111) or (100) n-GaAs: layer 1 n-AlxGa1-xAs (Sn), layer 2 thin active layer from a Ga-As-Si solution (<= about 1 um), layer 3 p-AlxGa1-xAs (Zn, about 1.5 um; about 1.8 um quoted for the heat estimate), layer 4 p-GaAs (Ge) contact layer; x about 0.2-0.4 from liquid concentrations; Zn-diffused p+ surface (about 0.2 um)
notes: Fab: first-person growth and preparation statements ('These modifications have enabled us to grow by liquid-phase epitaxy a structure', p.2; 'We have prepared lasers with a range of Si concentrations', p.3); all four authors at Bell Telephone Laboratories, Murray Hill (p.2) -> org_bell_labs under rule 12 (judgment, as smit1988 'We realised'). Mounting: Cr-Au p contact bonded to a Cr-Sn coated diamond on a Cu block; heat-sink temperatures are those of the Cu block (p.3). Layer thicknesses are Table I values for a typical run, varying by a factor of 2 across a wafer (p.3); the emission energy of this diode was 80 meV above that expected for GaAs, attributed to Al transfer into layer 2 (p.3). Not entered: square-diode and 560-um Fabry-Perot thresholds of 1000 / about 1600 A/cm2 at 300 K (p.2; other diodes, areas not stated; abstract prints 100 A/cm2 for the square diodes); highest CW heat-sink temperature 311 K of several diodes (270-311 K, p.3; no parameter); junction temperature about 25 K above the 297 K heat sink (author_estimate, no parameter); spectra of Fig. 3 (peak energies 1.433-1.449 eV labelled at 0.1-0.80 A dc; the lasing line at 0.82 A dc is shown with a width bound of 0.5 meV (3 Angstrom) but its energy is not labelled). Registry gap: threshold current density (A/cm2) has no parameter; the threshold currents here are derived from the printed densities and the stated diode size.

label: Distributed-feedback dye laser: rhodamine 6G in a 14 um gelatin film with induced index periodicity (about 0.3 um) on glass, transversely UV-pumped
core_material: dichromated gelatin film, holographically exposed (He-Cd UV interference pattern) and developed to a spatial index modulation, soaked in rhodamine 6G; 14 um thick; on a glass substrate
notes: Fab: 'Experimentally we have induced index periodicities in gelatin films' (p.2 abstract) and 'we have implemented and tested a DFB dye laser in a gelatin film' (p.3); both authors at Bell Telephone Laboratories, Holmdel -> org_bell_labs (rule 12 judgment, as smit1988). Pumped transversely by a nitrogen laser (UV), lasing above pump densities of 1e6 W/cm2 (p.4; intensity, no registry parameter). Scope judgment: a thin-film DFB laser on a glass substrate is treated as a chip-scale component (D411), not a bulk dye laser. Not entered: output linewidth < 0.5 Angstrom, the spectrometer resolution limit (p.4), stated for the first test laser before devices of several thicknesses are introduced, so its sample identity is not stated (D159) and it is an instrument bound; width about 0.1 mm of the first test laser (same identity issue); multiline spacing about 5 Angstrom of Fig. 3(b), attributed to film modes N = 3-5 (p.4; transverse film modes, not a cavity FSR); the 45 um film device of Fig. 3(c) (no value); rhodamine 6G fluorescence width about 50 Angstrom at 0.59 um in uniform gelatin (ref. 8, cited).
